Container.Name: GravityLAN
Container.Overview: GravityLAN is a self-hosted network radar, inventory, orbit topology mapper and rack planner for your homelab, with an optional Linux agent and in-browser SSH terminal.[br][br] [b]What GravityLAN does[/b][br] - Scans your subnets (Nmap and ARP) for hosts, open ports, services and vendors, keeps multi-VLAN routers as one device with multiple interfaces, supports shared IPVLAN MACs and flags unexpected MAC changes for controlled review.[br] - Models your network as an interactive orbit topology (with calculated single points of failure and backup paths) and as 19-inch or 10-inch racks with passive equipment, ports and cabling.[br] - Tracks reachability, latency, flapping, SSL expiry and pending security updates over 24 h, 7 d or 30 d, and provides a multi-tab browser SSH terminal with an encrypted key vault and password confirmation before sensitive actions.[br] - Optional integrations: lightweight Linux agent (CPU, RAM, disks, temperatures, Layer-2 ARP probe in routed VLANs, SSH package updates), read-only router subnet import (SNMP or UniFi), read-only Proxmox VE guest sync, webhooks (ntfy/Gotify presets) and scoped API tokens with a Python client.[br][br] [b]Persistent data & backups[/b][br] Data Storage (/mnt/user/appdata/gravitylan -> /app/data) holds the SQLite inventory (gravitylan.db), measurement history (telemetry.db), the encrypted secret key (ssh_vault.key) and automatic pre-migration database copies (data/backups/). The JSON export in Settings backs up inventory, topology, racks and general settings for host migration, but excludes passwords, tokens and SSH keys. Before upgrading, stop the container and copy the appdata directory (plus GRAVITYLAN_VAULT_KEY if configured externally).[br][br] [b]Important requirements[/b][br] - PUID 99 and PGID 100 (nobody:users): on start the container makes /app/data writable for this user and drops root privileges. No privileged mode needed (NET_RAW and NET_ADMIN in Extra Parameters suffice).[br] - Single instance: run only one GravityLAN container per appdata path. For lasting use and browser SSH sessions, access GravityLAN over HTTPS behind a reverse proxy.[br] - Network mode: [b]Host[/b] (default, recommended) gives full Layer-2 ARP/MAC visibility on all Unraid interfaces (WebUI at http://SERVER-IP:8000). Alternatively use [b]Custom: br0[/b] (macvlan/ipvlan) with a fixed IP, or add VLAN networks (br0.10, br0.20 ...) under "Additional Networks". [b]Bridge[/b] is not recommended because NAT hides MAC addresses. In routed subnets (L3 Routed), an agent with "L2 Subnet Scanner (Probe)" enabled can report MAC addresses.[br][br] [b]Documentation[/b][br] English README, German README (README.de.md) and Unraid guide (docs/unraid-template.md): https://github.com/SleeperXr/GravityLAN[br][br] [b]Deutsch[/b][br] GravityLAN ist ein selbst gehostetes Netzwerk-Radar, Inventar, Orbit-Topologie- und Rack-Planer fürs Homelab – mit optionalem Linux-Agenten und SSH-Terminal im Browser.[br][br] [b]Was GravityLAN macht[/b][br] - Scannt deine Subnetze (Nmap und ARP) nach Hosts, Ports, Diensten und Herstellern, führt Multi-VLAN-Router als ein Gerät mit mehreren Schnittstellen, unterstützt geteilte IPVLAN-MACs und meldet abweichende MAC-Adressen kontrolliert zur Prüfung.[br] - Zeichnet dein Netz als interaktiven Orbit-Netzplan (mit berechneten Single Points of Failure und Backup-Pfaden) sowie als 19- oder 10-Zoll-Racks mit passiven Einbauten, Ports und Verkabelung.[br] - Verfolgt Erreichbarkeit, Latenz, Flackern, SSL-Ablauf und offene Sicherheits-Updates über 24 h, 7 d oder 30 d und bietet ein Multi-Tab-SSH-Terminal im Browser mit verschlüsseltem Key-Store und Passwortbestätigung vor kritischen Aktionen.[br] - Optionale Integrationen: schlanker Linux-Agent (CPU, RAM, Laufwerke, Temperaturen, Layer-2-ARP-Probe in gerouteten VLANs, Paket-Updates per SSH), lesender Router-Subnetz-Import (SNMP oder UniFi), lesender Proxmox-VE-Abgleich, Webhooks (ntfy/Gotify) sowie gescopte API-Tokens und Python-Client.[br][br] [b]Persistente Daten & Backups[/b][br] Data Storage (/mnt/user/appdata/gravitylan -> /app/data) speichert das SQLite-Inventar (gravitylan.db), die Messdaten (telemetry.db), den Vault-Schlüssel (ssh_vault.key) und automatische Pre-Migrations-Kopien (data/backups/). Der JSON-Export in den Einstellungen sichert Inventar, Topologie, Racks und Einstellungen für einen Host-Umzug, enthält aber keine Passwörter, Tokens oder SSH-Keys. Vor einem Update den Container stoppen und den Appdata-Ordner kopieren (ggf. inkl. externem GRAVITYLAN_VAULT_KEY).[br][br] [b]Wichtige Anforderungen[/b][br] - PUID 99 und PGID 100 (nobody:users): Beim Start macht der Container /app/data für diesen Benutzer beschreibbar und gibt root-Rechte ab. Kein Privileged-Modus nötig (NET_RAW und NET_ADMIN in Extra Parameters reichen).[br] - Einzelinstanz: Nur einen GravityLAN-Container pro Appdata-Ordner betreiben. Für den Dauerbetrieb und Browser-SSH-Sitzungen HTTPS über einen Reverse Proxy nutzen.[br] - Netzwerktyp: [b]Host[/b] (Standard, empfohlen) bietet volle Layer-2-ARP-/MAC-Sicht auf allen Unraid-Schnittstellen (WebUI unter http://SERVER-IP:8000). Alternativ [b]Custom: br0[/b] (macvlan/ipvlan) mit fester IP oder zusätzliche VLANs (br0.10, br0.20 ...) unter "Additional Networks". [b]Bridge[/b] wird nicht empfohlen, da NAT die MAC-Adressen verbirgt. In gerouteten Subnetzen (L3 Geroutet) kann ein Agent als L2-Probe die MAC-Adressen liefern.[br][br] [b]Dokumentation[/b][br] Deutsche README (README.de.md), englische README und Unraid-Anleitung (docs/unraid-template.md): https://github.com/SleeperXr/GravityLAN

Container.Description:
GravityLAN is a self-hosted dashboard, network radar, topology mapper, and rack planner for your homelab or home network.
Features: - Discovery & Inventory: Scheduled Nmap and ARP subnet scans (hostnames, ports, services, vendors, multi-VLAN interfaces, IPVLAN support, and controlled MAC conflict review). - Orbit Topology & Racks: Interactive solar-system topology map with calculated single points of failure and 19"/10" rack planner with front/rear cabling. - Health & Availability: Reachability and latency history, SSL certificate expiry, and offline flap protection. - In-Browser SSH Terminal: Multi-tab web terminal with encrypted server-side key vault, host-key pinning, and step-up password confirmation. - Optional Integrations: Linux monitoring and patching agent (with Layer-2 ARP probe for routed VLANs), read-only router subnet import (SNMP / UniFi), read-only Proxmox VE guest sync, webhooks (ntfy / Gotify), and scoped API tokens with a Python client. - GravityUI: Vue 3 interface with Night, Starlight, Aurora, Day map, and custom JSON themes (EN / DE).
Note: GravityLAN uses host networking mode by default to ensure direct Layer-2 ARP detection and Nmap raw socket access across your local subnets without privileged mode.
Container.Changes:
### 0.8.0 - GravityUI only: the classic React interface is gone. New: Proxmox VE integration (VM and container names and addresses, optional adding to the dashboard, guests hung on their node), an app-wide search (Ctrl+K), a time zone setting, own designs plus the Aurora and Starlight themes, a second DNS server, an assistant that arranges the orbit map, and a notice when an agent stops reporting. Security: the setup wizard only scans private networks, the master token is stored as a hash and can be replaced under Settings → Access, and backups no longer contain credentials. The database is copied before a migration, log times follow TZ (tzdata in the image), and every Python package is pinned. Agent 0.3.15. Security hardening: WebSocket origin check, security headers, CSRF-safe agent config and scanner routes, tokens, submitted values and database passwords masked in logs; GRAVITYLAN_TRUSTED_PROXIES for the real client address behind a reverse proxy, with a warning when a proxy is not trusted or TZ is missing.
### 0.7.0 - GravityUI is the default interface; the classic React view stays one more release as a fallback and is removed after that. Audit log under Logs, and a password confirmation before terminals, agent actions, credential changes and backups. Persistent notification outbox with ntfy/Gotify presets, plus new-device and IP-change events with read tracking. Agent installer and SSH deploy verify SHA-256 checksums. Choose which devices are on the orbit map. Backups contain rack equipment, ports and cables. A backup can be restored in the setup wizard, and older databases and backups deduplicate and receive missing unique indexes automatically, with a copy of the database first. Images are built and published by CI. New tutorial for HTTPS with a reverse proxy.
### 0.6.0 - Racks rebuilt: faceplates that look like the hardware, drag and drop with snapping and undo, rack equipment (patch panels, UPS, power strips, blanks, cable management), ports and cables with a front and a rear view. Backup links and a resilience view on the orbit map, single points of failure on Health. Company demo network. Design critique fixes with a readable type floor, smooth dashboard scrolling, dnspython 2.9.0.
### 0.5.6 - Follow-ups to the 0.5.5 security fixes: install command uses the server URL and needs an explicit opt-in over HTTP, bounded live discovery, install codes and open streams revoked on import and reset. Backups include device interfaces. GravityUI overview leads with network status, names problem devices and has 44 px touch targets on phones. Agent 0.3.10.
### 0.5.5 - Security fixes from an external review (thanks @schaefer-informationstechnik): settings tokens can no longer reopen setup, safe service links, bounded scans, SSH host keys checked on agent deploy, no SSH fallback to the Docker host, clean backup imports, database reset revokes old access. The manual agent install needs HTTPS or ALLOW_INSECURE=1; new options Allow Insecure Agent Install and Docker Host IP.
### 0.5.4 - Tutorials page (DE/EN) for setup, VLANs, agents, SSH and Unraid; About page; default UI switch (React or GravityUI); security patch badges on the dashboard; phone and orbit map fixes.
### 0.5.3 - Docker: PUID and PGID (template: 99/100); the container makes the data directory writable for them on start, so a fresh appdata directory no longer stops it with a permission error.
### 0.5.2 - Deleting a device in GravityUI works again; scans pick up hostnames from mDNS, NetBIOS and the system resolver.
### 0.5.1 - Package updates accept a sudo password for key logins; GravityUI no longer reports sleeping clients as disrupted.
### 0.5.0 - GravityUI, a preview of the new interface, with every page of the classic view, an orbit map and racks.
Full changelog: https://github.com/SleeperXr/GravityLAN/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md

Config.Name: WebUI Port
Config.Description: The HTTP port on which the GravityLAN WebUI and REST API are served.

Config.Name: Data Storage
Config.Description: Directory to store persistent data (SQLite database, SSH key vault, backups). Use it for one GravityLAN container only. Backup, restore and the database reset in Settings need this SQLite database.

Config.Name: Internal Port
Config.Description: Container internal listening port (matches WebUI port).

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the server runs as. On start the container makes the Data Storage directory writable for it. Unraid default: 99 (nobody).

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the server runs as. Unraid default: 100 (users).

Config.Name: Allow Insecure Agent Install
Config.Description: Let the manual agent install command (curl | sudo bash) download over plain HTTP without ALLOW_INSECURE=1. The agent runs as root and its token travels unencrypted, so only enable this on a trusted network. Better: an HTTPS server URL behind a reverse proxy, or SSH deploy.

Config.Name: Docker Host IP
Config.Description: LAN IP of this Unraid server. Only SSH logins (agent deploy, updates, terminal) to this address may retry over the Docker bridge gateway, needed when the container can't reach its own host, e.g. with macvlan. Leave empty if not needed.

Config.Name: Secure Cookies
Config.Description: Mark the session cookie Secure. Turn on only once you open GravityLAN over HTTPS (reverse proxy); over plain HTTP the browser drops the cookie and the login does not stick.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxies
Config.Description: Behind a reverse proxy: its IP addresses or networks, comma-separated (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 or 192.168.1.5). Only these may set the client address with X-Forwarded-For, so the login limit, the audit log and agent IPs see the real client instead of the proxy. Leave empty without a proxy.

Config.Name: Extra Origins
Config.Description: Only needed if your reverse proxy rewrites the Host header and sends no X-Forwarded-Host: the address you open GravityLAN with, as a JSON list such as ["https://gravity.example.com"]. Otherwise WebSockets (live scan, logs, metrics, terminal) refuse the page. Leave empty otherwise.

Config.Name: Debug Mode
Config.Description: Enable detailed logging for debugging scanner and backend issues.
